# Cantrip.Content

Loading `.cantrip` files: the library a game hands the runtime, and the definitions in it.

Part of [the API reference](README.md). The guides are [docs/csharp.md](../csharp.md) and [docs/godot.md](../godot.md); when something here surprises you, [docs/troubleshooting.md](../troubleshooting.md) is the other end of it.

| Type | |
|---|---|
| [`BoardMetric`](#boardmetric) | How the distance between two slots is measured. |
| [`BoardShape`](#boardshape) | The shape of the board a battle is fought on: a rectangle of `lanes` across and `ranks` along the facing axis, both counting from 0. Content declares any number of them by name and a game picks one per battle; content that declares none gets `BoardShape.Default`, which is the board every game had before boards existed. |
| [`BoardSides`](#boardsides) | Whether the two sides stand on mirrored grids or on one shared grid. |
| [`ContentLibrary`](#contentlibrary) | Every definition loaded from DSL files. Parse errors are collected rather than thrown, so a designer sees all the problems in a folder at once. Reloading a file replaces exactly the definitions that file contributed, which is what makes hot reload cheap. |
| [`EnemyPatternKind`](#enemypatternkind) | *Undocumented.* |
| [`EntityDefinition`](#entitydefinition) | Loaded, validated content: one card, status, relic, enemy, keyword or resource. Built once from the syntax tree and shared by every entity instantiated from it. |
| [`MoveDefinition`](#movedefinition) | A named enemy move: `move "Chomp": deal 11 to player`. |
| [`OnVacated`](#onvacated) | What happens to the actors behind a slot when its occupant leaves. |
| [`PhaseDefinition`](#phasedefinition) | A behaviour phase: `phase Broken when hp <= max_hp / 2`. Moves tagged with the phase are available only while its condition holds. |
| [`Reach`](#reach) | How far an action reaches, in slots on the board: `range 1` is everything up to one step away — melee — and `range 2..3` is a bow that cannot shoot point blank. |
| [`ResourceRule`](#resourcerule) | Bounds and reset behaviour for a stat treated as a resource. Resources are data, declared with `resource "energy"`; common ones are built in. |
| [`ScenarioDefinition`](#scenariodefinition) | A `scenario` block together with the file it came from. |
| [`StatusFlags`](#statusflags) | Status flags: what a status is (buff, debuff) and how it behaves (persistent, unique). |
| [`TestDefinition`](#testdefinition) | A `test` block together with the file it came from. |
| [`VerbDefinition`](#verbdefinition) | A content-defined verb: `verb shatter(t): ...`. |

## BoardMetric

```csharp
public enum BoardMetric
```

How the distance between two slots is measured.

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `Manhattan = 0` | The two terms added. A diagonal step is two. |
| `Chebyshev = 1` | The larger of the two terms. A diagonal step is one. |

## BoardShape

```csharp
public sealed class BoardShape
```

The shape of the board a battle is fought on: a rectangle of `lanes` across and `ranks` along the facing axis, both counting from 0. Content declares any number of them by name and a game picks one per battle; content that declares none gets `BoardShape.Default`, which is the board every game had before boards existed.

A shape is content, never something a game invents at runtime, because the linter has to know the depth to say that `it.rank <= 3` on a two-rank board matches nothing.

### Constructors

```csharp
public BoardShape(string name, int lanes = 1, int ranks = 0, BoardSides sides = Facing, BoardMetric metric = Manhattan, OnVacated onVacated = Gap, string? laneWord = null, string? rankWord = null)
```

*Undocumented.*

### Fields and constants

```csharp
public const string DefaultName = "default"
```

The name of the board content gets when it declares none.

```csharp
public const int Unbounded = 0
```

`BoardShape.Ranks` when a lane goes on for as long as anything is put in it.

### Properties

```csharp
public static BoardShape Default { get; }
```

`lanes 1, ranks unbounded, facing, manhattan, gap`: today's board, spelled out. It is what content that declares no board is played on, which is why no sample moves.

```csharp
public bool LaneHoldsOne { get; }
```

Whether a lane on this board holds one actor at most, which is true of a board one rank deep: `lane(who)` is then `who` alone, however it is written.

```csharp
public string LaneWord { get; }
```

What this game calls a lane, for rules text. `lane` unless content says.

```csharp
public int Lanes { get; }
```

Slots across. One or more.

```csharp
public int? MaxDistance { get; }
```

The greatest number of steps this board can put between two actors, or null when the ranks are unbounded and there is no such number. A reach of this much or more reaches everybody, which is what CT332 says out loud.

On a `facing` board the two sides are mirrored and the rank term across them is `a.rank + b.rank + 1`, so the deepest pair is the two back ranks facing each other: `2 * (Ranks - 1) + 1`. On a `shared` board a rank is one place for everybody, so it is `Ranks - 1`.

```csharp
public BoardMetric Metric { get; }
```


*Undocumented.*

```csharp

```

*Undocumented.*

```csharp
public bool RankHoldsOne { get; }
```

Whether a rank on this board holds one actor at most, which is true of a board one lane wide — today's board, and so worth saying out loud when content writes `rank(who)` on it and gets a group of one.

```csharp

```

What this game calls a rank, for rules text. `rank` unless content says.


Slots deep, or `BoardShape.Unbounded` for a lane with no floor.

## BoardSides

```csharp
public enum BoardSides
```

Whether the two sides stand on mirrored grids or on one shared grid.

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `Facing = 0` | Each side has its own grid, rank 0 nearest the middle. Two actors on opposite sides at rank 0 are one step apart, and a rank never means the same place on both sides. |
| `Shared = 1` | One grid, shared. A rank is the same place whoever is standing on it. |

## ContentLibrary

```csharp
public sealed class ContentLibrary
```


*Undocumented.*

```csharp
public DiagnosticBag LoadFile(string path)
```

Reads a file from the file system. Tools and desktop games use this; a game engine that packs content into an archive (Godot's `res://`, for one) cannot, because this goes through `File`. Such a host reads the text its own way and calls `ContentLibrary.LoadText(string, string)`, which is the only seam that needs no file system at all.

```csharp
public DiagnosticBag LoadFolder(string folder, string extension = ".cantrip", bool recursive = true)
```

Loads every matching file under a folder, in ordinal path order for determinism. Like `ContentLibrary.LoadFile(string)`, this reads the real file system, so a packed game must do its own discovery and call `ContentLibrary.LoadText(string, string)` per file, keeping the same ordinal order.

```csharp
public DiagnosticBag LoadText(string text, string file)
```

Parses and registers a source file. Returns that file's diagnostics.

```csharp
public IReadOnlyList<EntityDefinition> Pool(string kind)
```

First match among several kinds, in the order given.

`ContentLibrary.Definitions` enumerates a dictionary, and a reload removes then re-adds its entries, so its order is not a contract and must never reach the RNG. Anything that picks content at random reads it from here instead, or the same seed would stop replaying.

```csharp
public ResourceRule? Resource(string stat)
```

*Undocumented.*

```csharp
public void Unload(string file)
```

Removes everything a file contributed.

## OnVacated

```csharp
public enum OnVacated
```

What happens to the actors behind a slot when its occupant leaves.

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `Gap = 0` | Nothing. The hole stays until something fills it, and survivors never move. |
| `CloseRanks = 1` | Everyone behind it in that lane steps forward one rank. |

## PhaseDefinition

```csharp
public sealed class PhaseDefinition
```

A behaviour phase: `phase Broken when hp <= max_hp / 2`. Moves tagged with the phase are available only while its condition holds.

### Constructors

```csharp
public PhaseDefinition(string name, ExprNode condition, SourceSpan span, bool retelegraph = false)
```

*Undocumented.*

### Properties

```csharp
public ExprNode Condition { get; }
```

Evaluated against the enemy each time its intent is rolled.

```csharp
public string Name { get; }
```

*Undocumented.*

```csharp
public bool Retelegraph { get; }
```

Whether entering this phase re-rolls the enemy's intent there and then, so a boss can telegraph the move the phase has just unlocked.

Opt-in, because it trades away a guarantee worth keeping: ordinarily the intent shown during the player's turn is exactly the move that follows, and re-telegraphing means a boss can change its mind after the player has committed. Only a phase that asks for it does that.

```csharp
public SourceSpan Span { get; }
```

*Undocumented.*


## Reach

```csharp
public struct Reach : IEquatable<Reach>
```

How far an action reaches, in slots on the board: `range 1` is everything up to one step away — melee — and `range 2..3` is a bow that cannot shoot point blank.

A reach is measured with `GameState.Distance(Entity, Entity)` between whoever is using the action and the candidate, and it is the only thing the `range` modifier channel changes: the channel computes `Reach.Max` and `Reach.Min` follows it down, so `modify range: set 1` makes a longbow melee rather than leaving it unable to reach anything at all.

### Constructors



